subject: Community Health
stem: A nurse is teaching a healthy 65-year-old client about recommended vaccines. Which vaccine should the nurse recommend annually?

options.feedback: Correct. Influenza vaccine is recommended every year.
Incorrect. Td is given every 10 years.
Incorrect. MMR is not given annually to adults.
Incorrect. Hepatitis B is a series, not annual.

rationale: The influenza vaccine is recommended annually for all adults, especially older adults.

subject: Pediatrics
stem: At which age does a nurse expect a healthy infant to sit without support?

options.feedback: Incorrect. Too early for unsupported sitting.
Correct. Infants typically sit unsupported around 6 months.
Incorrect. Children usually walk around this age.
Incorrect. This is well past the expected milestone.

rationale: Sitting without support is an expected milestone around 6 months of age.

subject: Maternity
stem: A nurse teaches a client planning pregnancy about preventing neural tube defects. Which supplement should the nurse emphasize?

options.feedback: Correct. Folic acid reduces the risk of neural tube defects.
Incorrect. Vitamin C does not prevent neural tube defects.
Incorrect. Vitamin D supports bone health, not neural tube closure.
Incorrect. Calcium supports bone development, not neural tube closure.

rationale: Folic acid taken before and during early pregnancy reduces neural tube defect risk.

subject: Community Health
stem: A nurse counsels a 55-year-old woman about routine screening. Which screening test is recommended for breast cancer detection?

options.feedback: Correct. Mammography screens for breast cancer.
Incorrect. Colonoscopy screens for colorectal cancer.
Incorrect. A Pap smear screens for cervical cancer.
Incorrect. This screens for osteoporosis.

rationale: Mammography is the standard screening test for early breast cancer detection.

subject: Pediatrics
stem: A nurse teaches new parents about infant nutrition. Until what age is exclusive breastfeeding generally recommended?

options.feedback: Correct. Exclusive breastfeeding is recommended for about the first 6 months.
Incorrect. Far too early to add other foods.
Incorrect. Solids are usually introduced around 6 months.
Incorrect. This exceeds the exclusive breastfeeding period.

rationale: Exclusive breastfeeding for about the first 6 months is recommended before introducing solids.

subject: Community Health
stem: A client who smokes asks about the benefit of quitting. Which is an accurate statement the nurse can share?

options.text: Quitting lowers the risk of lung cancer and heart disease
options.feedback: Correct. Cessation reduces multiple health risks.

options.text: Quitting has no benefit after age 50
options.feedback: Incorrect. Benefits occur at any age.

options.text: Switching to light cigarettes eliminates risk
options.feedback: Incorrect. Light cigarettes still carry risk.

options.text: Damage from smoking cannot be reduced by quitting
options.feedback: Incorrect. Quitting improves health outcomes.

rationale: Smoking cessation reduces the risk of lung cancer, heart disease, and other conditions at any age.

subject: Community Health
stem: A nurse teaches an adult client about physical activity. Which weekly amount of moderate aerobic activity is generally recommended?

options.feedback: Correct. About 150 minutes per week is recommended.
Incorrect. This is well below the recommendation.
Incorrect. This exceeds the standard recommendation.
Incorrect. Regular activity is important.

rationale: At least 150 minutes of moderate aerobic activity per week is recommended for adults.

subject: Pediatrics
stem: A nurse teaches parents of a toddler about injury prevention. Which action best reduces the risk of accidental poisoning?

options.text: Store cleaning products in a locked cabinet
options.feedback: Correct. Locking away toxic substances prevents poisoning.

options.text: Keep medications on the kitchen counter
options.feedback: Incorrect. This increases access risk.

options.text: Allow the toddler to explore under the sink
options.feedback: Incorrect. This exposes the child to hazards.

options.text: Store chemicals in unlabeled drink bottles
options.feedback: Incorrect. This causes accidental ingestion.

rationale: Storing toxic substances in locked cabinets prevents accidental poisoning in toddlers.

subject: Maternity
stem: A nurse teaches a postpartum client warning signs to report. Which finding should the client report to the provider?

options.feedback: Correct. This suggests infection and must be reported.

options.text: Gradual decrease in lochia over days
options.feedback: Incorrect. This is expected.
Incorrect. These are normal.
Incorrect. This is expected.

rationale: Foul-smelling lochia with fever indicates possible postpartum infection and must be reported.

subject: Community Health
stem: A nurse reviews a client's body mass index (BMI) of 27. How should the nurse classify this result?

options.feedback: Correct. A BMI of 25 to 29.9 is classified as overweight.
Incorrect. Underweight is below 18.5.
Incorrect. Normal is 18.5 to 24.9.
Incorrect. Obesity begins at 30.

rationale: A BMI of 25 to 29.9 falls in the overweight category.

subject: Community Health
stem: A nurse plans client teaching. Which factor indicates the client is ready to learn?

options.text: The client asks questions about self-care
options.feedback: Correct. Curiosity signals readiness to learn.

options.text: The client is in severe acute pain
options.feedback: Incorrect. Pain interferes with learning.
Incorrect. Sedation impairs learning.

options.text: The client refuses to discuss the diagnosis
options.feedback: Incorrect. This suggests a barrier.

rationale: A client who asks questions about self-care demonstrates readiness to learn.

subject: Community Health
stem: A nurse teaches a client about skin cancer prevention. Which recommendation is appropriate?

options.text: Apply broad-spectrum sunscreen before sun exposure
options.feedback: Correct. Sunscreen reduces UV-related skin damage.

options.text: Use tanning beds instead of natural sunlight
options.feedback: Incorrect. Tanning beds increase skin cancer risk.

options.text: Avoid sunscreen to allow vitamin D formation
options.feedback: Incorrect. Sun protection is still recommended.

options.text: Sunburn is harmless if it fades
options.feedback: Incorrect. Sunburns increase cancer risk.

rationale: Broad-spectrum sunscreen and sun protection reduce the risk of skin cancer.

subject: Community Health
stem: A nurse teaches an adult client about reducing cardiovascular risk. Which lifestyle recommendations should the nurse include? Select all that apply.

options.text: Eat a diet low in saturated fat and sodium

rationale: Physical activity, a heart-healthy diet, and tobacco avoidance reduce cardiovascular risk.

subject: Pediatrics
stem: A nurse educates parents about well-child care. Which are components of a routine well-child visit? Select all that apply.

options.text: Only visits when the child is ill

rationale: Well-child visits include growth assessment, immunizations, and anticipatory guidance.

subject: Maternity
stem: A nurse teaches a pregnant client about healthy behaviors during pregnancy. Which instructions are appropriate? Select all that apply.

options.text: Take a prenatal vitamin with folic acid daily
Take medications without checking with the provider

rationale: Prenatal vitamins, alcohol avoidance, and regular prenatal visits promote a healthy pregnancy.

subject: Community Health
stem: A nurse teaches an older adult about preventing falls at home. Which recommendations should the nurse include? Select all that apply.

options.text: Install grab bars in the bathroom
Keep walkways dark to save energy

rationale: Removing hazards, installing grab bars, and improving lighting reduce fall risk in older adults.

subject: Community Health
stem: A nurse reviews recommended screenings for an adult client. Which are routine preventive screenings? Select all that apply.

options.text: Routine brain MRI for all adults

rationale: Blood pressure, cholesterol, and depression screenings are routine adult preventive measures.

subject: Pediatrics
stem: Which 2 behaviors are expected developmental milestones for a healthy 3-year-old child?
rationale: A 3-year-old typically speaks in short sentences and can ride a tricycle.

subject: Community Health
stem: Colorectal cancer screening is generally recommended to begin at age 45 for average-risk adults.
rationale: Average-risk colorectal cancer screening is recommended starting at age 45.

subject: Pediatrics
stem: A mild low-grade fever after a routine childhood vaccine is an absolute contraindication to future immunizations.
rationale: A mild fever after vaccination is a common, expected response and is not a contraindication.

subject: Pediatrics
stem: For each developmental milestone, click to indicate the age group in which it is typically first achieved.
rationale: Rolling and first words emerge in infancy; stair-climbing and spoon-feeding emerge in toddlerhood.

subject: Community Health
stem: For each health maintenance activity, select all age groups for which it is routinely recommended.
rationale: Influenza vaccine and blood pressure screening apply broadly, while routine pneumococcal vaccination targets older adults.

subject: Maternity
stem: The nurse teaches that a pregnant client should take {1} daily to help prevent neural tube defects and should avoid {2} entirely during pregnancy.
rationale: Folic acid prevents neural tube defects; alcohol should be avoided completely during pregnancy.

subject: Community Health
stem: Highlight the behaviors that promote health during a routine wellness visit. The client reports [[exercising 30 minutes most days]], [[smoking one pack of cigarettes daily]], [[eating vegetables with most meals]], and [[skipping all preventive checkups]].

chunks.text: smoking one pack of cigarettes daily

rationale: Exercise and a vegetable-rich diet promote health, while smoking and skipping checkups do not.

subject: Community Health
stem: Complete the diagram for a client at risk for cardiovascular disease by selecting health-promoting actions, the goal, and outcomes to monitor.
rationale: Exercise and a low-sodium diet reduce cardiovascular risk, monitored by blood pressure and weight.

subject: Community Health
stem: The nurse teaches that adults should aim for at least [1] of moderate aerobic activity per week and should include [2] on two or more days weekly.
rationale: Adults should get at least 150 minutes of moderate aerobic activity plus muscle-strengthening exercise weekly.

subject: Community Health
stem: A nurse plans a health-promotion teaching session for a client. Place the steps of the teaching process in the correct order.
